Q-1.name: Availability and legality
Q-1.criterion: all section 4 bytes obtainable; section 3.7 licence position recorded

target_T.note: byte-verified into the models container by the predecessor study; not re-acquired

jlens_code.note: installed into the frozen image from the pinned commit

secondary_benchmark.reason: gated auto; the deciding data file returns HTTP 401 unauthenticated and no token exists on the execution host
secondary_benchmark.resolved_at: P-0, before any model call, before any outcome was observed
secondary_benchmark.why_not_a_failure: section 4.3 registers the fallback in advance precisely for this case; taking a pre-registered fallback at the pre-registered time is the criterion being satisfied, not evaded

licence_position_recorded.position: research use; no adapter weight byte and no repository source file redistributed, not into Git, not to any public location, not into the handoff container

Q-2.name: Immutable hashes
Q-2.criterion: every acquired file hashed on the execution host and matching its authoritative value before use; content-addressed into models/sha256/<aa>/<full>; round-trip re-hash after upload

authority_kinds_used.lfs_sha256: the origin's LFS object id, which is the content sha256, compared directly
authority_kinds_used.git_blob_sha1: for non-LFS files the origin publishes only a git blob id, a sha1 over b'blob <len>\0'+content; the host recomputes that same construction

Q-2.why_two_kinds: a git blob id is not a content sha256; treating one as the other is the silent mismatch this gate exists to catch, so they are stored in separate fields and verified by separate code paths
Q-2.deduplication_note: 13 files were already present at their content-addressed path, which is expected because the two adapter repositories share byte-identical tokenizer and template files. A pre-existing blob is verified by HEAD plus a full round-trip re-hash rather than by issuing a PUT, so benign deduplication does not trip hard blocker 12.6 and nothing is overwritten.
Q-2.mirror_route_disclosure: the GPU host cannot reach the HuggingFace origin, so bytes were fetched through a mirror; the mirror is never trusted, because every file is checked against an authority obtained from the origin and a failing file is deleted rather than uploaded

claim_ceiling: Q-1 and Q-2 are engineering gates. Passing them establishes that the registered bytes exist, were obtained byte-exactly and are addressable. It establishes nothing about J-space, about distillation, or about reasoning, and it is not a scientific result.
